stories.title: Ratko Mladic, ex-Bosnian Serb warlord who oversaw atrocities, dies in prison at 84
stories.summary:
Ratko Mladic, the former Bosnian Serb general known as the “butcher of Bosnia,” has died at age 84 while serving a life sentence for war crimes. U.N. officials said he died in a prison hospital in the Netherlands, where he had been held by the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia.

Mladic was convicted in 2017 of genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity during the 1992-95 wars in the former Yugoslavia. His forces were responsible for shelling Sarajevo and carrying out what has been described as the worst massacre in Europe since World War II.

The news was reported by multiple outlets, including Al Jazeera, BBC, Breitbart and The Washington Times, all confirming his death while incarcerated.

stories.title: Top secrets come spilling out
stories.summary:
The Zimmermann Telegram, a coded message sent by German Foreign Minister Arthur Zimmermann in 1917, has long been cited as a pivotal moment that helped draw the United States into World War I. British analysts successfully deciphered the communication, which was intended for a German diplomat in Mexico.

The intercepted message proposed an alliance with Mexico against the United States. It included a promise to help Mexico reconquer lost territories in Texas, New Mexico, and Arizona if the U.S. entered the conflict.

Additionally, the telegram outlined plans to resume unrestricted submarine warfare.

When the contents of the telegram became public, it caused a significant sensation in American media and political circles. The revelation shifted public opinion and provided a strong impetus for the United States to join the war against Germany.

links.headline: Top secrets come spilling out
links.excerpt: In 1917, British analysts deciphered a coded message the German foreign minister sent to one of his country's diplomats vowing to begin "unrestricted submarine warfare" and seeking to win over Mexico with a promise to "reconquer the lost territory in Texas, New Mexico and Arizona" if the US entered the world war. When it became public, the Zimmerman Telegram caused a sensation, helping propel the US into the conflict against Germany.

The renaming comes amid escalating trade tensions between the United States and Canada. Trump said the U.S. has long been disadvantaged in cross-border trade and defense arrangements, arguing that Canada has benefited from American support while failing to reciprocate fairly.

Officials framed the action as part of a broader effort to assert U.S. interests during ongoing negotiations with Canadian counterparts.

stories.title: Queensland concedes law imposing mandatory jail on some offenders as young as 10 breaches human rights
stories.summary:
Queensland has conceded that a law imposing mandatory jail terms on some offenders as young as 10 breaches human rights. The state government introduced the legislation as part of a broader law and order crackdown.

Under the bill, offenders who commit a serious crime while on bail face a mandatory minimum 12 months in prison. The measure is designed to address perceived failures in the current bail system.

However, the government acknowledges that the laws raise the risk of overcrowding in jails. One expert has warned that the legislation may lead to “cruel outcomes” for young offenders.

stories.title: An $18bn settlement is a drop in the ocean for Meta – but the tide will still come for it | Chris Stokel-Walker
stories.summary:
Meta has agreed to an $18 billion settlement with 52 US attorneys general over claims that its products were designed in ways that harmed children. The agreement resolves the state lawsuits without admitting liability, a move described as pragmatic for the company.

Despite the size of the payment, commentators suggest the sum is relatively small compared with Meta’s overall financial position. The settlement does not appear to end legal pressure on the platform owner.

Further lawsuits are expected around the world, indicating that regulatory and legal challenges may continue despite this resolution.

stories.title: Solons want budget of PCO, attached agencies like IBC, restored
stories.summary:
The House of Representatives has filed its P7.2-trillion 2027 budget bill, placing the spending plan under congressional scrutiny.

Leaders and members submitted the measure on Wednesday, with approval expected by final reading in October. Rep. Mikaela Suansing, who heads the House appropriations committee, filed the bill.

Separately, lawmakers have asked the appropriations committee to restore the original 2027 budget requested by the Presidential Communications Office and its attached agencies, including the Information Bureau. They argued that these offices play a crucial role in countering misinformation.

stories.title: Sprains, pain, and whiplash: Waymo and Zoox test drivers are getting hurt as robotaxis scale
stories.summary:
Test drivers for Waymo and Zoox have sustained more than two dozen injuries in 2024 and 2025, according to a TechCrunch review of data submitted to the Occupational Safety and Health Administration.

The injuries included sprains, pain, and whiplash resulting from hard braking or other sudden movements made by the autonomous vehicles. The incidents occurred as robotaxi operations scaled.

stories.title: The White House’s plan to vet potentially dangerous AI is cloaked in secrecy
stories.summary:
The White House has finalized a framework for testing new artificial intelligence models, but the plan is being kept largely private. The Trump administration developed the guidelines after months of discussions with tech industry leaders.

The framework focuses on assessing safety and cybersecurity risks associated with emerging AI systems. However, officials have not released detailed information about how the vetting process will work.

Critics argue that the lack of transparency undermines public accountability and could benefit secretive AI companies. The decision leaves many open questions about the scope and effectiveness of the proposed testing regime.

stories.title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda
stories.summary:
A pro-Israel messaging website operating under the name of a nonexistent US think tank has published more than 560,000 words in nine days, according to Guardian analysis. The site produced 124 reports intended to shape AI chatbots toward making pro-Israel arguments.

The content was built on a commercial platform that promises to optimize material so AI systems will cite it. The website presents Israel’s position on various subjects while using the branding of an institution that does not exist.

stories.title: ‘Never seen this level of objection’: Scotland pushes back against datacentre boom
stories.summary:
Scotland is pushing back against a wave of large datacentre proposals, with officials describing an unprecedented level of local objection. The Guardian reports that Holyrood is “inching towards moratorium” as concerns mount over the scale and impact of planned developments.

The most prominent case involves Auchtertool in Fife, where a real estate consultancy plans to build a facility described as larger than the village itself. The proposed datacentre would stand 35 metres high and cover an area bigger than 100 football pitches.

Billed as potentially the second-biggest datacentre in the world, the Auchtertool project has drawn 1,600 objections. The article frames the dispute as part of a broader Scottish resistance to rapid expansion in the sector.

stories.title: Vholume review – a headlong rush of parkour perfection in a brutalist wonderland
stories.summary:
Vholume is a PC parkour game that asks whether its breathless design feels curated or crafted. The review describes it as an exhilarating rush through impossible dystopian cityscapes, built around wall-runs, death-chancing leaps and split-second improvisation.

The Guardian’s review frames the game as austere yet polished, with a moveset reminiscent of Mirror’s Edge. Its level names draw on terms such as “conapt,” suggesting an influence from earlier urban-futurist references.
